newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Fino, parties resume crisis talks on Albania vote.
newsitem.headline: Fino, parties resume crisis talks on Albania vote.

text.p: Prime Minister Bashkim Fino plunged into fresh talks on Wednesday to end a crisis jeopardising planned elections as a deadline set by European envoy Franz Vranitzky slipped by.

Vranitzky had warned Albania's politicians to solve a deadlock over electoral ground-rules by the end of Tuesday or face the risk of losing international aid needed to overcome near-anarchy afflicting the poor Balkan country.

Late-night efforts by Fino yielded no agreement but he began a new round of negotiations with parties in his so-called national unity government on Wednesday morning, politicians who asked not to be identified said.
"It is up to the parties to decide what to do with this argument (over rules)," one of Fino's spokesmen said.

Fino was desperately trying to convince the parties in his government to run in the election, which they have threatened to boycott over regulations they say favour President Sali Berisha's former ruling Democratic Party.
The vote is regarded as the most important first step in restoring order to Albania, torn apart by a popular anti-Berisha insurrection involving riots and looting in March.
Fino met Berisha late on Tuesday and the president agreed to amend some of the rules for the election, aides to the prime minister said.
There was still no reaction from the parties on Wednesday whether the changes were enough for them to join the vote.
Vranitzky said time was running out for Albania after Fino failed to solve the crisis in marathon talks on Monday.

"Time is running out. The government of national reconciliation, the prime minister and the president must reach agreement today," Vranitzky said in a statement after talks in Vienna on Albania with U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan.
Amid intense Western concern, Italy and Greece have added their voices to the chorus of warnings from governments.
Albania is still tense after the wave of riots and looting in February and March when thousands of people lost their money in the collapse of crooked pyramid investment schemes.
Vranitzky has made five fruitless mediating trips to Albania since the unrest began and could return this week.
Fino appealed to the West for help to solve the crisis and spoke with Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi, Vranitzky and U.S. Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum.
Italy, leading a multinational force protecting humanitarian aid, on Tuesday called again for political compromise and Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta said the next 24 hours were very important.

Greece said failure to reach an election compromise would jeopardise the continued presence of the 6,000-strong troop force. Western countries have already warned they may cut aid to Albania unless elections go ahead.
